title: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares: the most squares of order n
keeper: Handbook of Combinatorial Designs, Table 3.87 (R. J. R. Abel, C. J. Colbourn and J. H. Dinitz), as in SageMath's MOLS_handbook_data, with the later results of families/mols/literature.json
revision: SageMath src/sage/combinat/designs/MOLS_handbook_data.py as of commit 7a10747217c3 (31 Jan 2025, the last change to the file), read through the GitHub API on 15 Nov 2026 (SHA-256 in source_sha256)

template.title: Mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order {n}
template.statement: Find as many mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order {n} as possible: Latin squares that, taken two at a time and superimposed, show each of the {n}^2 ordered pairs of symbols exactly once. N({n}) is not known.
template.submission: Text file: K Latin squares of order {n} one after another, each {n} rows of {n} symbols 0..{n_minus_1} (or 1..{n}) separated by spaces; '#' starts a comment; an optional first line "{n} K". Or an ({n}, K + 2; 1) difference matrix: a first line "group n_1 ... n_r" (an abelian group Z_n1 x ... x Z_nr of order {n}), then K + 2 rows of {n} elements written as integers 0..{n_minus_1} in mixed radix. See checkers/mols_check.py.

score: K, the number of mutually orthogonal Latin squares (larger is better)
best_text: The best known lower bound is N({n}) >= {best} ({holder}); {best_plus_1} squares would improve it.
bound_source: N(n) <= n - 1, with equality exactly when a projective plane of order n exists; N(n) <= n - 2 when the Bruck-Ryser theorem excludes a plane of order n
holder_sources: the Handbook table (constructions in its Section III.3) and literature.json
open_rule: every order n that is not a prime power, n > 6 (N(n) is known only for prime powers and n = 6), with n >= 500 or a value for n < 500 known from literature.json; a submission is the squares or a difference matrix
left_out: 1273 prime powers (N(n) = n - 1); n = 10 (the single problem mols-10); 348 other orders below 500 whose current value is in the 2024 compilation, which could not be read (the paper is open access; to be read by hand)
